concepts.title: Introduction to Normalization
concepts.summary: Eliminate Insertion, Deletion, and Update anomalies by decomposing flawed tables using Functional Dependencies.
concepts.definition_text: Normalization & Functional Dependency (X -> Y): Schema refinement decomposing tables using functional dependencies to remove redundancy and anomalies. Normalization is the systematic process of structuring relational tables to remove data redundancy and prevent Insertion, Update, and Deletion Anomalies. It relies on Functional Dependencies (`X -> Y`, meaning `X` uniquely determines `Y`) and lossless-join decompositions across Normal Forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF).
concepts.example_text: Separating `departments(dept_id, dept_name, building)` from `students` so renaming a building updates 1 row instead of 5,000. Example: SELECT s.full_name, d.dept_name, d.building FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.dept_id = d.dept_id LIMIT 5;

concepts.title: Third Normal Form (3NF)
concepts.summary: Eliminate Transitive Dependencies (A -> B -> C) so non-key attributes depend directly on the key and nothing else.
concepts.definition_text: Third Normal Form (3NF): 2NF relation with no transitive dependencies between non-prime attributes. A relation is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF AND has NO Transitive Dependencies—where a non-prime attribute determines another non-prime attribute (`student_id -> dept_id -> dept_building`). Moving `(dept_id, dept_building)` to `Departments` achieves 3NF.
concepts.example_text: Moving `dept_name` and `building` out of `Students` into `Departments` removes `student_id -> dept_id -> building`. Example: SELECT dept_id, dept_name, building FROM departments;
